_comment: Per-airline complaint submission channel metadata, read by letter-fit.py. Only verified facts belong here: every char_limit carries limit_verified + limit_source. Unverified fields are the literal string 'unknown' so letter-fit.py flags them at runtime instead of quietly assuming. To add an airline, copy an existing block and fill in what you have — an entry with char_limit: null is still useful for its channel_notes.

_counting_methods.codepoints: Python len() — one character per Unicode codepoint.
_counting_methods.utf8_bytes: Length of the UTF-8 encoding. Non-ASCII (em-dash, smart quotes) costs 2-3.
_counting_methods.crlf: Codepoints with every newline expanded to a CRLF pair.
_counting_methods.html_entities: Codepoints after HTML-escaping the specials a rich-text field would encode.
_counting_methods.unknown: Not established for this form. letter-fit.py takes the worst of the above and multiplies by an inflation factor — see UNKNOWN_INFLATION_DEFAULT in letter-fit.py.

WN.name: Southwest Airlines

web_form.observed_inflation_source: 2026-06-13: the live form's counter read 2798 for a letter whose Python len() was 2472 (ratio 1.132, rounded up). No standard encoding reproduces the form's number — UTF-8 bytes 2482, CRLF 2495, HTML entities 2500 — so the factor stands in for an unidentified counting method.

WN.channel_notes: The form's counter runs materially higher than any plain encoding of the same text. Treat 2500 as a budget to stay well under, not to fill.
